meta.name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi First-Year Costs
meta.excerpt: Corgis have become expensive to buy, with IVDD being the key health cost to plan for. Here's the honest year-one breakdown.
meta.meta_description: Pembroke Welsh Corgi first-year cost breakdown: purchase price, vet care, IVDD risk planning, pet insurance, and ongoing annual costs.

hero.alt: Adult Pembroke Welsh Corgi relaxing at home in a family setting

intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: What a Pembroke Welsh Corgi Actually Costs Year One
intro.html: Corgi purchase prices have risen significantly with the breed's popularity — $1,000–$2,500 from reputable breeders is now standard. Ongoing costs are moderate for a small-to-medium breed. The key health cost to plan for is IVDD — the elongated Corgi spine combined with food-motivated weight gain creates a meaningful long-term risk that insurance helps manage.

health.heading: IVDD and Other Major Costs

IVDD risk is significantly reduced by maintaining a healthy weight. An obese Corgi is dramatically more vulnerable to disc herniation than a lean one. Portion control is your most effective IVDD prevention tool.

special.label: What to Know
special.heading: Why Corgis Are More Expensive Than They Used to Be
special.html:
Internet fame and Royal family association drove Corgi demand sharply upward over the past decade. Reputable breeders with health-tested stock and waiting lists now price at $1,500–$2,500. Be wary of Corgis priced significantly below this from breeders who can't provide OFA and PRA documentation — the health savings may cost more in vet bills than the price difference suggests.

Insurance is especially worth having for Corgis given the IVDD risk. Apply before the first vet visit.

faq.q: How much does a Corgi cost per year?
faq.a: After first-year setup: $1,500–$2,500 annually. Food is small-to-medium breed portioned; insurance is the main recurring cost. Years with an IVDD episode will be significantly higher — which is exactly why insurance matters for this breed.

faq.q: Should I get pet insurance for a Pembroke Welsh Corgi?
faq.a: Yes. IVDD is a meaningful risk for Corgis, and surgery runs $3,000–$8,000. Insurance at $50–$80/month is the right trade for that certainty. Apply before the first vet visit.

Lower acquisition cost ($200–$400 adoption fee). Some rescue Corgis have known IVDD history — get a health disclosure and factor this into insurance decisions. Adult Corgis from rescue can be excellent family dogs.

faq.q: What furniture modifications should I make for a Corgi?
faq.a: Ramps for the couch and bed if you allow them up — repeated jumping on and off furniture is a meaningful IVDD contributor for Corgis. Ramps are inexpensive ($30–$80) and reduce the cumulative spinal load over years. This is especially important once the dog is past middle age.
